MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The washer assortment feels like a natural next purchase because it complements my metric bolts and nuts and helps spread fastening loads across project materials.",
    "Rubber grommets complement my drilling supplies by protecting wires through holes, while removable tape and tool organizers support the assembly work and growing tool collection reflected in my recent purchases."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Crucible tongs assume I am melting metal, but my recent tools support drilling, fastening and repairs; working with metal does not mean I need furnace equipment.",
    "A pH meter measures something I have no current reason to test, and bakery bags do not help with my workshop projects.",
    "Wood screws and epoxy fit my interests, but I already bought screw assortments and a gallon of resin. That makes another purchase less urgent unless I need a particular size or have run out."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in tools seems to have been stretched into an interest in specialized equipment without a matching project.",
    "Some suggestions repeat materials I have purchased without distinguishing between something I already have and something that adds a useful capability."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Compatibility matters: washers that fit my metric hardware are immediately useful, whereas white wood screws or wire connectors require a specific size, finish or wiring need.",
    "My recent purchases make complementary supplies appealing, especially items that help finish, protect or organize work done with the tools I already own.",
    "I buy tools and supplies frequently, but that does not mean I need to replenish every material or start an unrelated kind of project."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The suggestions recognize my ongoing DIY and repair work, but sometimes miss the difference between a useful project complement, a duplicate supply and equipment for an unrelated task."
}
